sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioners that they are the son and daughter respectively of Late Pramod Singh who is one of the legal heirs of Thakur Raghunath Singh who was the original owner of the ancestral house.
Raghunath Singh had six sons.

One of them was Kunwar Digvijay Singh alias K.D.
Singh Babu.

4. The State Government is intending to acquire House no. C-215 situated at Civil Lines K.D. Singh Babu Marg, Qasba and Tehsil ? Nawabganj, District - Barabanki to set up a National Museum in the name of K.D. Singh Babu.
5. The petitioners are in possession of their share of property which they derived out of their father Shri Pramod Singh's share.

Kunwar Raghunath Singh was late Great Grandfather of Shri Pramod Singh as Pramod Singh was the son of Kunwar Umesh Singh and Kunwar Umesh Singh was son of Kunwar Bhupendra Singh one of the six sons of Thakur Raghunath Singh.
6. The petitioners have 1/18 th share of the total area of the house, i.e., 3274 square meters in which the petitioner's share is 181.89 square meters.
7. A suit for partition was collusively filed by Smt. Divya Shahi daughter of Kunwar Umesh Singh which was decided without impleading the petitioners or their father as defendants.
The aforesaid R.S. No.645 of 2006 being decided in a collusive manner the petitioners came to know about the illegal compromise after execution proceedings were filed in execution case no.7/2009.

8. The petitioners have filed their objections to the said execution case on 02.3.2024 and taking into account the objections of the petitioners the Civil Court has stayed the proceedings of the execution case till further orders.

The petitioners are co-sharers and they were not impleaded as defendants in R.S. No.645/2006.
9.
Similarly, petitioners have not been heard and the decision has been taken by the Government to acquire the aforesaid house for establishing a National Museum as aforesaid.
There are 44 co-sharers of the property.
The house is still unpartitioned.

10. Learned Standing Counsel on the basis of copy of the plaint that was filed in R.S. No.645/2006 before the Civil Court for the partition has stated that father of the petitioner Kunwar Pramod Singh was one of the parties in the said regular suit.

11. Learned Standing Counsel has produced before this Court instructions dated 07.8.2024 sent by the District Magistrate, Barabanki wherein it has been stated that Shri K.D. Singh Babu was a Hockey player of international fame and was also awarded Padam Shri by the Central Government.
The State Government wishes to honour his memory by establishing a National Museum in the house in which he was born and brought up.
The said house is in a dilapidated condition.

2 12.

The State Government by its decision dated 10.7.2024 has asked the Department of Culture to acquire the property either on the basis of mutual consent in terms of Government Order dated 19.3.2015 by getting executed sale deeds of various co-sharers of the property or by moving a proposal for acquisition.
13. It has been stated in the said instructions that the petitioners have no locus to challenge such a decision of the State Government as they are not yet share holders of the house in question.

Their father Shri Pramod Singh is still alive and he has already given an affidavit in favour of the proposal made by the Government for acquiring the property by giving compensation in terms of the new Land Acquisition Act.
14. Along with the instructions details of persons who have given their affidavit has been enclosed.
There are 19 persons who have already given their affidavits including Pramod Kumar Singh son of Umesh Singh, the father of the petitioners.
The proposal to acquire the house in question and to set up a memorial/ museum in the memory of Shri K.D. Singh Babu shall only be given effect to after following due procedure prescribed in law.
15. The instructions are kept on record.

16. We are of the considered opinion that the petitioners have neither challenged the State Government decision dated 10.7.2024 nor has disclosed correct facts in the writ petition as their father who is the actual co-sharer of the property has been shown to have died and the petitioners in their representation to the District Magistrate, copy of which has been filed as annexure to the writ petition have stated that they are entitled to a share in the property on the basis of Mitakshara, line of descent/succession in Hindu Law whereas it is doubtful whether Mitakshara principle would apply in properties situated in U.P.
17.
Writ petition is dismissed.
18. It will be open for the petitioner to file fresh petition with correct pleadings for challenging the Government Order dated 10.7.2024 as aforesaid.
